nodes.title: Cloud fundamentals: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Every cloud certification starts with the same vocabulary: IaaS / PaaS / SaaS, public / private / hybrid, capex vs opex, elasticity, regions and AZs. Getting these right is half the foundational exam.

flashcards.front: IaaS vs PaaS vs SaaS — pick an example of each.
flashcards.back: IaaS (Infrastructure): EC2, Azure VM, Compute Engine — you manage OS and up. PaaS (Platform): App Engine, Elastic Beanstalk, App Service — you manage code, provider manages runtime. SaaS (Software): Gmail, Salesforce — you just use it. As you go up the stack, you get convenience, lose control.

flashcards.front: Region vs Availability Zone — what's the difference?
flashcards.back: A region is a geographic area (us-east-1, europe-west2). An AZ is one or more data centers inside a region with independent power/cooling/network. AZs in a region are connected by low-latency fiber but isolated from each other's failures. Best practice: spread workload across 2-3 AZs for HA.

flashcards.front: Elasticity vs scalability — different things?
flashcards.back: Scalability: the system can be grown (add capacity to handle 10x load). Elasticity: it auto-shrinks back when load drops — you don't pay for idle capacity. A scalable system isn't necessarily elastic (a manually-resized DB is scalable but not elastic). Cloud's killer feature is being both.

flashcards.front: Capex vs opex — why does cloud favor opex?
flashcards.back: Capex (capital expenditure): big upfront purchase (a server, a building). Opex (operating expenditure): ongoing per-unit cost (cloud usage, electricity). Cloud turns infrastructure into opex — no $500k server purchases, just monthly bills. Easier for finance to scale, easier to abandon a project without sunk cost.

questions.q: A startup wants to avoid large upfront hardware purchases and instead pay only for the IT capacity it actually consumes each month. Which financial model best describes this approach?
choices: Capital expenditure (CapEx), where assets are purchased up front and depreciated over their useful life
Operational expenditure (OpEx), where IT capacity is billed periodically based on consumption
Fixed-asset depreciation, an accounting treatment that spreads a purchase cost over multiple years
Total cost of ownership (TCO), a planning metric that aggregates all costs of owning an asset
questions.explanation: Consumption-based cloud billing is treated as an operational expenditure (OpEx): the customer is billed periodically for what they use rather than buying the hardware up front. CapEx is the opposite — large up-front asset purchases. Depreciation is an accounting mechanism, not a pricing model. TCO is a comparison metric that sums every cost (people, power, hardware, software), not a billing approach a provider charges.

questions.q: An organization wants its email, file storage, and collaboration tools to be fully managed by the provider, with no servers to install or patch. Which cloud service model fits this requirement?
choices: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), where the customer manages the operating system, runtime and applications on provider VMs
Platform as a Service (PaaS), where the customer brings application code while the provider runs the OS and runtime
Software as a Service (SaaS), where the provider runs the whole application stack
Function as a Service (FaaS), where the customer uploads individual functions and the provider runs them on demand
questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 is delivered as Software as a Service (SaaS): Microsoft operates the entire stack — infrastructure, platform, and the applications themselves — and the customer simply signs in. IaaS still leaves operating-system patching to the customer, PaaS still leaves application code and updates with the customer, and FaaS is a developer-focused execution model for event-driven functions, not a full collaboration suite.

questions.q: A regulated bank wants to keep some workloads on-premises for compliance reasons while running other workloads in the public cloud, with both connected through secure networking. Which deployment model best describes this configuration?
choices: Public cloud only, with all systems hosted by a provider and shared with other tenants
Hybrid cloud, combining on-premises infrastructure with public cloud resources through secure connectivity
Private cloud only, with dedicated hardware operated exclusively for the bank in its own datacentre
Community cloud, where multiple organizations with shared concerns operate a jointly governed environment
questions.explanation: Hybrid cloud is the deployment model that joins on-premises (private) infrastructure with public cloud, connected by secure networking so workloads and data can flow between them — exactly what a regulated bank needs. Public cloud only places everything off-premises. Private cloud only leaves out the public-cloud half. Community cloud is a shared environment between multiple organizations with the same regulatory or mission profile, which is different from a single bank's mixed estate.

questions.q: A retailer experiences holiday traffic that is 10x higher than normal. They want services to automatically add capacity during peak hours and shrink afterward. Which cloud characteristic provides this behavior?
choices: Elasticity, the ability to automatically add and remove capacity in response to demand
Geo-redundancy, the property of having data replicated across geographically separate regions
Multitenancy, where many customers share the same underlying platform with logical isolation
High availability, the design goal of keeping a service reachable despite component failures
questions.explanation: Elasticity is the cloud characteristic that automatically scales resources up under load and back down when demand falls. Geo-redundancy is about replication across regions for disaster recovery, not auto-scaling. Multitenancy describes how the platform shares infrastructure between customers. High availability is about keeping a service reachable through failures, not adjusting capacity to match traffic.

questions.q: A marketing team wants to build a simple low-code app to track event registrations without writing custom backend code. Which component of the Power Platform should they use?
choices: Power BI, which builds interactive dashboards and reports over a data model
Power Automate, which builds workflows that connect apps and trigger actions
Power Apps, which builds low-code business applications with forms and logic
Power Pages, which builds external-facing public websites backed by Dataverse
questions.explanation: Power Apps is the low-code app-building service in the Power Platform — ideal for an internal event-registration tracker. Power BI is for analytics and dashboards. Power Automate is the workflow engine that connects services. Power Pages is for public, external-facing websites, not the simple internal tool described.

questions.q: A developer wants a single REST API to read Outlook calendar, OneDrive files, and Teams chats with one access token. Which Microsoft service exposes this unified API?
choices: Microsoft Graph, a unified REST endpoint that exposes data across Microsoft 365 and Entra ID
Azure Logic Apps, a workflow service that orchestrates connectors but is not itself a single API
Power Automate connectors, packaged adapters used inside Power Automate flows
Microsoft 365 Defender API, a security-only endpoint scoped to incidents and alerts
questions.explanation: Microsoft Graph is the unified REST API that gives developers access to mail, calendar, files, chats, identities and more across Microsoft 365, Entra ID and Windows from a single endpoint and token. Logic Apps is a workflow orchestrator, not a unified data API. Power Automate connectors are pre-packaged adapters used inside flows. The Microsoft 365 Defender API only covers security data such as incidents, alerts and threat hunting.

questions.q: An organization is migrating a CRM workload to a public cloud provider that exposes virtual machines, virtual networks, and storage that the customer manages. Which cloud service model is being consumed?
choices: Software as a Service (SaaS), where the provider runs the entire application stack
Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), where the provider exposes VMs, networks and storage
Platform as a Service (PaaS), where the provider runs the OS and runtime and the customer brings code
Function as a Service (FaaS), where the provider runs individual event-driven functions
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) exposes virtualized compute, network and storage; the customer is still responsible for the operating system, middleware and applications running on top. SaaS hides everything from the customer. PaaS lets the customer bring only code on a managed runtime. FaaS runs only individual functions, not whole VMs and networks.

nodes.title: Microsoft Purview: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Microsoft Purview is the data governance, compliance, and protection suite for Microsoft 365 and beyond — classification, data loss prevention, retention, eDiscovery, and insider risk. It's the compliance counterpart to the security stack.

flashcards.front: What is sensitivity labelling?
flashcards.back: Sensitivity labels classify and protect content (e.g. Confidential) and can enforce encryption, watermarks, and access restrictions that travel with the file. Labels can be applied manually or automatically based on content (e.g. detecting credit-card numbers).

flashcards.front: What does Data Loss Prevention (DLP) do?
flashcards.back: DLP detects sensitive information (PII, financial data) across email, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, and endpoints, and enforces actions — block, warn, or require justification — to stop it leaving the organisation. Policies are built from sensitive-info types.

flashcards.front: What is retention vs deletion in Purview?
flashcards.back: Retention policies and labels keep content for a required period (compliance) and/or delete it after a period (minimising risk). They resolve conflicts by a precedence order — retention generally wins over deletion to preserve records.

flashcards.front: What is eDiscovery used for?
flashcards.back: eDiscovery finds, holds, and exports content relevant to investigations or litigation across Microsoft 365. Legal holds preserve content in place so it can't be altered or deleted while a case is active.

questions.q: An information-protection team wants to apply labels such as 'Confidential' or 'Public' to Word documents so encryption and watermarks are automatically enforced when the file is shared. Which Microsoft Purview feature provides this?
choices: Microsoft Purview retention policies, which control how long content is kept or deleted
Insider Risk Management, which surfaces risky user activities such as data exfiltration
Sensitivity labels (Microsoft Purview Information Protection), which classify and protect content
Communication Compliance, which monitors messages for policy violations in regulated environments
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview Information Protection sensitivity labels classify content and apply encryption, watermarks and access restrictions that travel with the document. Retention policies focus on keeping or deleting content. Insider Risk Management surfaces risky activities such as exfiltration but does not label files. Communication Compliance reviews messages for policy violations.

questions.q: A company must prevent users from emailing files containing credit card numbers to external recipients. Which Microsoft Purview capability enforces this rule across Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams?
choices: Data Loss Prevention (DLP), which inspects content and blocks risky shares
Customer Lockbox, which gates Microsoft engineer access to tenant data
eDiscovery (Standard), which searches and exports content for legal matters
Conditional Access app control, which adds session-level controls on user sign-ins
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview DLP inspects content for sensitive information types (credit-card numbers, SSNs, etc.) and blocks, warns or audits attempts to share them in Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams. Customer Lockbox governs Microsoft engineer access. eDiscovery is for legal-hold and content search. Conditional Access app control adds session-level signals through a reverse proxy but isn't the data-classification engine.

questions.q: Lawyers need to place certain mailboxes and SharePoint sites on legal hold and search across them for case-related content. Which Microsoft Purview feature is designed for this workflow?
choices: Records Management retention labels, which classify and dispose of records on a schedule
eDiscovery, which places content on hold and searches across mailboxes and sites for legal matters
Communication Compliance, which monitors messages for policy violations
Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management, which inventories software vulnerabilities on devices
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (Standard and Premium) is built for legal teams: place custodians and locations on hold, search across Exchange, SharePoint and Teams, and export results for case work. Records Management focuses on retention/disposition. Communication Compliance is for message review. Defender Vulnerability Management inventories software flaws on devices — not legal evidence.

questions.q: An organization wants HR managers to be alerted when employees download abnormally large amounts of data shortly before resigning. Which Microsoft Purview solution targets this scenario?
choices: eDiscovery (Standard), which searches and exports content for legal cases
Communication Compliance, which scans messages for harassment or policy violations
Records Management, which classifies content as records and enforces retention
Insider Risk Management, which surfaces risky user activities such as data exfiltration
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management correlates signals such as data exfiltration, sensitive downloads and HR system events (like resignation indicators) to flag risky user activity while preserving privacy. eDiscovery is for legal-matter search. Communication Compliance scans messages, not data movement. Records Management is about retention of records, not anomalous user behavior.

questions.q: Two business divisions inside the same tenant must be prevented from communicating in Teams to avoid conflicts of interest. Which Microsoft Purview feature enforces this segregation?
choices: Conditional Access policies, which gate user sign-in but do not block intra-tenant chat between divisions
Information Barriers, which block specified user groups from communicating in Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive
Communication Compliance, which reviews messages after the fact instead of preventing them
Sensitivity labels, which classify and protect documents and emails rather than blocking chats
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview Information Barriers enforce policies that prevent specified user groups from communicating or collaborating across Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive — used heavily in finance and legal. Conditional Access gates sign-in but doesn't segregate chat between two groups inside the same tenant. Communication Compliance reviews messages, it doesn't prevent them. Sensitivity labels protect documents, not chat sessions.

questions.q: Which Microsoft 365 feature lets administrators automatically delete user mailboxes and SharePoint content after a defined retention period to meet records management policies?
choices: OneDrive Files On-Demand, which controls how files are downloaded to a device, not how long they are kept
Conditional Access session controls, which limit a user's session rather than retain content
Microsoft Purview retention policies and retention labels, which keep or delete content on a schedule
Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management, which tracks software vulnerabilities on devices
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview retention policies and retention labels automatically keep or delete content across Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams based on configured rules, which is exactly what records-management policies require. Files On-Demand affects offline sync, not lifecycle. Conditional Access session controls limit sign-in sessions. Defender Vulnerability Management is about software vulnerabilities on devices.

nodes.title: Microsoft Intune: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Intune is Microsoft's cloud-based endpoint management service for mobile device management (MDM) and mobile application management (MAM), unifying device and app control through the Microsoft Intune admin center. The MD-102 and MS-102 exams test enrollment, compliance, configuration profiles, app protection, and Conditional Access integration.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between a compliance policy and a configuration profile in Intune?
flashcards.back: A compliance policy defines rules a device must meet (encryption, OS version, no jailbreak) and reports a compliant/non-compliant state; a configuration profile pushes actual settings (Wi-Fi, VPN, restrictions, certificates) onto the device. Compliance evaluates, configuration enforces settings.

flashcards.front: What does an app protection policy (APP/MAM) protect without requiring device enrollment?
flashcards.back: It protects data inside managed apps at the app level — controlling cut/copy/paste, save-as, encryption, and PIN access to corporate data — so it works on unenrolled BYOD devices (MAM-without-enrollment).

flashcards.front: How does Intune compliance integrate with Conditional Access?
flashcards.back: Intune reports each device's compliance state to Microsoft Entra ID; a Conditional Access policy can then require a compliant (or Entra hybrid-joined) device before granting access to apps like Exchange or SharePoint, blocking non-compliant devices.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of device enrollment in Intune?
flashcards.back: Enrollment registers a device with Intune so it can receive MDM management — applying policies, profiles, and apps. Methods include Windows Autopilot, Apple Automated Device Enrollment (ADE), and Android Enterprise enrollment.

questions.q: An IT admin must enroll new corporate Windows laptops so they auto-configure with company apps, settings, and policies the first time the user signs in. Which Microsoft service supports this scenario?
choices: Group Policy preferences, which require devices to be domain-joined and on the corporate network
Windows Update for Business, which controls how Windows feature and quality updates are deployed
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint onboarding, which adds devices to the EDR/AV portal
Windows Autopilot, which provides zero-touch first-boot provisioning
questions.explanation: Windows Autopilot, used with Microsoft Intune, gives new devices a zero-touch first-boot experience: they join Entra ID and download apps, policies and settings automatically. Group Policy requires a domain-joined device on the corporate network and is not a cloud zero-touch service. Windows Update for Business manages updates only. Defender for Endpoint onboarding adds an existing device to the EDR service, but it does not provision the laptop end-to-end.

questions.q: A user needs a personal, persistent Windows 11 desktop in the cloud they can access from any device, billed per user per month at a fixed rate. Which Microsoft offering best fits?
choices: Windows 365 Cloud PC, a per-user, dedicated, fixed-price Windows desktop in the cloud
Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD), a flexible, Azure consumption-billed desktop platform for IT-managed deployments
Microsoft Dev Box, a developer-focused workstation with build tools rather than a general personal desktop
Azure Bastion, an Azure service that provides secure RDP/SSH access to VMs through the portal
questions.explanation: Windows 365 provides a personal Cloud PC at a predictable fixed per-user, per-month price — exactly the brief. Azure Virtual Desktop is more flexible (multi-session, pooled, personal) but is billed on Azure consumption rather than fixed per-user pricing. Microsoft Dev Box is a developer workstation product, not a general personal desktop. Azure Bastion is only a jump-host for secure RDP/SSH access to other VMs.

questions.q: An IT manager wants only managed corporate phones that are enrolled and compliant to access Microsoft 365 mail. Which Microsoft service enforces device enrollment and compliance policies?
choices: Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager, which scores regulatory compliance posture
Microsoft Entra Permissions Management, which governs cloud entitlements and least-privilege access
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, which performs endpoint detection and response on already-managed devices
Microsoft Intune, which enrolls devices and enforces MDM/MAM compliance policies
questions.explanation: Microsoft Intune is the unified endpoint management service that enrolls devices and enforces compliance policies before they reach corporate resources. Compliance Manager scores regulatory posture, not device state. Entra Permissions Management focuses on cloud entitlements. Defender for Endpoint provides EDR on devices that are already managed; it doesn't enroll them.

questions.q: A sales rep using a personal phone needs to read corporate email but the company refuses to fully manage the device. Which Intune feature lets the company protect data inside the Outlook app without controlling the whole device?
choices: Mobile Device Management (MDM) full enrollment, which places the entire device under company management
Mobile Application Management (MAM) with app protection policies, which protect data inside specific apps only
Conditional Access location policies, which restrict access by network or country but do not protect in-app data
BitLocker drive encryption, which encrypts Windows volumes and does not apply to mobile apps
questions.explanation: Intune App Protection Policies (MAM without enrollment) let the company govern data inside managed apps such as Outlook, OneDrive and Teams while leaving the rest of the personal device alone. MDM full enrollment is exactly what the user refuses — control over the whole device. Conditional Access location rules limit where sign-ins succeed but do not protect data inside an app. BitLocker is a Windows volume-encryption feature, unrelated to mobile app data.

questions.q: An IT manager wants to provide a managed Windows 11 multi-session environment in Azure where multiple users share the same VM, paying only for the compute they consume. Which Microsoft offering best fits?
choices: Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD), which supports Windows 11 multi-session and is billed on Azure consumption
Microsoft Dev Box, a developer workstation product rather than a multi-session desktop platform
Windows 365 Cloud PC Enterprise, a per-user, fixed-price personal Cloud PC
Microsoft Intune Cloud PC, which is not an existing Microsoft offering
questions.explanation: Azure Virtual Desktop supports Windows 11 multi-session and is billed on Azure consumption (compute, storage, networking) — exactly the multi-user, pay-for-what-you-use brief. Microsoft Dev Box is a developer workstation. Windows 365 Cloud PC is per-user, dedicated, fixed-price. 'Microsoft Intune Cloud PC' is not a real Microsoft offering.

nodes.title: Compliance frameworks: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Compliance is the discipline of mapping your controls to an external framework (PCI, HIPAA, SOC 2, GDPR, ISO 27001) and proving it to an auditor. Most exam questions test which framework owns which scope, not the minutiae of each clause.

flashcards.front: PCI DSS — what's the scope?
flashcards.back: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard. Applies to anyone who stores, processes, or transmits cardholder data (PAN, expiry, CVV). 12 high-level requirements: firewalls, no defaults, encrypted storage, encrypted transmission, antivirus, secure dev, restrict access, MFA, log, test, policy. Required by Visa/Mastercard, not by law.

flashcards.front: HIPAA vs HITRUST — what's the difference?
flashcards.back: HIPAA is U.S. law for protected health information (PHI) — sets the legal requirements but is high-level on technical controls. HITRUST CSF is a certifiable framework that operationalizes HIPAA (plus ISO, NIST, PCI) into specific testable controls. Healthcare orgs are legally HIPAA-bound; many also pursue HITRUST cert to prove diligence.

flashcards.front: SOC 2 — what's it certify?
flashcards.back: American Institute of CPAs report on a SaaS company's controls across five trust criteria: security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, privacy. Type I = controls designed at a point in time. Type II = controls operated effectively over 6-12 months. Enterprise customers ask for the Type II as proof you're not making it up.

flashcards.front: GDPR — what does it require beyond US-style privacy laws?
flashcards.back: European General Data Protection Regulation. Requires explicit consent (not pre-ticked), right to access / deletion / portability, 72-hour breach notification, data protection officer (for large processors), data minimization, and Privacy Impact Assessments for high-risk processing. Fines: up to 4% of global revenue. Applies to anyone processing EU residents' data, regardless of company location.

questions.q: An organization wants to track how employees adopt Microsoft 365 services (Teams meetings, OneDrive sharing, Outlook usage) to drive change-management initiatives. Which feature in the admin center surfaces this information?
choices: Microsoft Secure Score, a security-posture rating in the Defender portal
Service Trust Portal, a public location for compliance audit documents
Adoption Score, which measures how the organization uses M365
Service Health Dashboard, which reports ongoing incidents and advisories
questions.explanation: Adoption Score (formerly Productivity Score) is the admin-center insight that measures how the organization uses Microsoft 365 services and highlights opportunities to improve adoption. Secure Score measures security posture, not usage. The Service Trust Portal exposes audit documents. The Service Health Dashboard reports incidents and advisories — not usage.

questions.q: An organization wants to ensure that even Microsoft engineers cannot access the tenant's data without explicit customer approval. Which Microsoft 365 feature provides this assurance?
choices: Service Trust Portal, which exposes audit reports and trust documents
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager, which scores regulatory compliance posture
Customer Lockbox, which gates Microsoft engineer access with customer approval
Service Health Dashboard, which reports current service incidents and advisories
questions.explanation: Customer Lockbox places a tenant approval step in front of any Microsoft support engineer's access to customer content, giving the customer the final say. The Service Trust Portal hosts audit documents — it does not gate engineer access. Compliance Manager measures posture. The Service Health Dashboard reports incidents and is not an access-control feature.

questions.q: A compliance officer needs a dashboard that maps the tenant's controls to regulations such as GDPR, ISO 27001, and HIPAA, with improvement actions and a compliance score. Which Microsoft service provides this?
choices: Microsoft Sentinel, the cloud-native SIEM that ingests security signals
Microsoft Defender XDR, the unified security operations portal
Microsoft Service Trust Portal, where audit reports and trust documents are published
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager, which maps controls to regulations
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager maps Microsoft- and customer-managed controls to frameworks such as GDPR, ISO 27001 and HIPAA, surfaces improvement actions and computes a compliance score. Sentinel is a SIEM. Defender XDR is a security-incident portal. The Service Trust Portal publishes audit reports but doesn't track per-tenant control state.

questions.q: An auditor asks for Microsoft's latest SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate for Microsoft 365. Where can the customer download these documents directly?
choices: Microsoft 365 admin center → Health → Service health, which reports current incidents
Microsoft Service Trust Portal, the central location for independent audit reports and certificates
Azure Marketplace → Compliance offers, where third-party compliance products are listed
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager → Solutions, which is for control assessments rather than audit downloads
questions.explanation: The Microsoft Service Trust Portal is the official location to download independent audit reports (SOC 1/2/3, ISO 27001, PCI), compliance white papers and trust documentation. Service health reports operational incidents. Azure Marketplace lists third-party offers. Compliance Manager runs control assessments but is not where the certificate PDFs are downloaded.

questions.q: Microsoft 365 customers worried about regulatory compliance can review independently audited reports and certifications. Which Microsoft service provides these reports along with trust documents and white papers in a single portal?
choices: Microsoft 365 admin center → Reports → Usage, which surfaces tenant usage data rather than audit reports
Microsoft Service Trust Portal, the single portal for audit reports, certificates and trust documents
Microsoft Defender XDR portal, the security incidents and threat-management console
Microsoft Secure Score portal, which rates security posture rather than publishing audit reports
questions.explanation: The Microsoft Service Trust Portal centralizes audit reports (SOC, ISO, PCI), GDPR documentation, white papers and other trust resources for customer compliance assessments. Admin-center usage reports show tenant activity, not third-party audits. The Defender XDR portal handles security incidents. Secure Score rates posture but does not publish audit reports.

nodes.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Microsoft Defender for Cloud (formerly Security Center + Azure Defender) is a Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) and Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP) for Azure, multi-cloud, and hybrid environments.

flashcards.front: CSPM vs CWPP — what does each do in Defender for Cloud?
flashcards.back: CSPM: continuously assesses security posture, assigns a Secure Score, and recommends remediations. CWPP: detects and responds to active threats on workloads (VMs, containers, DBs).

flashcards.front: Secure Score — what does it measure?
flashcards.back: A percentage representing how many of Defender's security recommendations you have implemented. Higher = better posture. Each recommendation has a point value.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint vs Defender for Cloud?
flashcards.back: Defender for Endpoint: EDR agent for individual Windows/Linux devices. Defender for Cloud: posture management and threat protection for cloud infrastructure.

flashcards.front: Defender for Cloud coverage beyond Azure?
flashcards.back: Supports AWS and GCP workloads via multicloud connectors, and on-premises servers via Azure Arc — providing a unified security view across environments.

questions.q: Which Microsoft Defender XDR component is specifically designed to detect lateral movement and credential theft against on-premises Active Directory domain controllers?
choices: Microsoft Defender for Office 365, which protects mail and collaboration tools
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, which performs EDR on workstations and servers
Microsoft Defender for Identity, which monitors on-prem AD traffic for credential attacks
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, the CASB that monitors SaaS app usage
questions.explanation: Microsoft Defender for Identity (formerly Azure ATP) ingests on-prem Active Directory traffic and detects credential-theft and lateral-movement techniques like Pass-the-Hash, Pass-the-Ticket and Golden Ticket. Defender for Office 365 protects mail/collab. Defender for Endpoint is EDR on individual devices. Defender for Cloud Apps is a SaaS CASB — none of those three is focused on AD domain-controller traffic.

questions.q: A company wants to scan inbound email attachments and links for phishing and malware before users click them. Which Microsoft Defender component provides Safe Attachments and Safe Links?
choices: Microsoft Defender for Office 365, which provides Safe Attachments and Safe Links
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, which provides EDR and anti-malware on the device itself
Microsoft Defender for Identity, which monitors on-prem AD traffic for credential attacks
Microsoft Defender for Cloud, which assesses Azure and multicloud resource posture
questions.explanation: Defender for Office 365 ships Safe Attachments (detonation of attachments in a sandbox), Safe Links (URL rewriting and time-of-click checks) and anti-phishing policies for Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive. Defender for Endpoint protects the device after a user already clicked. Defender for Identity watches on-prem AD. Defender for Cloud is for Azure and multicloud workload posture, not user inboxes.

questions.q: An admin wants visibility into shadow IT — unsanctioned cloud apps employees use from corporate devices — and the ability to block risky ones. Which Microsoft service provides this CASB capability?
choices: Microsoft Defender for Servers, which protects Windows and Linux server VMs from malware and exploits
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, the CASB that discovers, scores and governs SaaS app usage
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, which provides EDR on individual devices
Microsoft Sentinel, the cloud-native SIEM that ingests signals from many sources
questions.explanation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps is Microsoft's Cloud Access Security Broker: it discovers shadow IT, scores each app's risk and can govern or block unsanctioned SaaS apps. Defender for Servers protects server VMs from malware. Defender for Endpoint is EDR on user devices. Sentinel ingests logs and alerts but is a SIEM/SOAR, not a CASB.

questions.q: An admin wants a numeric measurement of the Microsoft 365 tenant's security posture and recommended actions to improve it. Which Microsoft service provides this score?
choices: Microsoft Secure Score, which rates the tenant's security posture
Adoption Score, which measures how the organization uses Microsoft 365 services
Microsoft Compliance Manager score, which rates regulatory and compliance posture
Productivity Score, the legacy name for Adoption Score before Microsoft renamed it
questions.explanation: Microsoft Secure Score, in the Microsoft Defender portal, gives a numeric rating of tenant security posture and ranks improvement actions. Adoption Score measures usage of M365 services. Compliance Manager scores regulatory posture, not security. Productivity Score was renamed to Adoption Score and is not a security metric.

questions.q: Which Microsoft service is a cloud-native SIEM and SOAR solution that ingests signals from Microsoft 365, Entra ID, and third-party sources to detect and respond to threats at scale?
choices: Microsoft Sentinel, the cloud-native SIEM and SOAR service in Microsoft's security portfolio
Microsoft Defender for Cloud, which assesses cloud workload posture across Azure and multicloud
Microsoft Compliance Manager, which scores regulatory compliance posture
Microsoft Purview Audit, which retains and surfaces unified audit log data
questions.explanation: Microsoft Sentinel is the cloud-native Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) and Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR) service that ingests signals from M365, Entra ID and many third-party sources. Defender for Cloud is for cloud workload posture, not log ingestion at scale. Compliance Manager is a compliance-posture tool. Purview Audit is a log archive, not a detection platform.

nodes.title: Microsoft 365 licensing: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Microsoft 365 is sold in subscription plans that bundle productivity apps, security, and device management. MS-900 exams test which plan includes which features and the volume licensing options.

flashcards.front: Microsoft 365 Business vs Enterprise plans — key split?
flashcards.back: Business plans (Basic/Standard/Premium) are capped at 300 users. Enterprise plans (E1/E3/E5) have no user cap and include advanced compliance and security features.

flashcards.front: What does Microsoft 365 E5 add over E3?
flashcards.back: E5 adds advanced security (Defender for Identity, Defender for Cloud Apps), advanced compliance (Purview), and Power BI Pro — roughly doubles the cost of E3.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Volume Licensing vs Microsoft 365 subscription?
flashcards.back: Volume Licensing (EA, CSP) offers negotiated pricing, centralised management, and payment flexibility for large organisations; subscriptions are per-user/month via direct or partner channels.

flashcards.front: Difference between Microsoft 365 and Office 365?
flashcards.back: Office 365 is the older brand for productivity apps + cloud services. Microsoft 365 adds Windows 10/11 Enterprise licences and advanced security/compliance tools.

questions.q: An organization with 200 employees needs Microsoft 365 desktop apps, Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, and Intune device management at a low per-user price. Which plan is the most cost-effective fit?
choices: Microsoft 365 Business Premium, designed for SMBs up to 300 seats with Intune and Defender
Microsoft 365 E5, the top enterprise SKU with advanced security and compliance
Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise, which includes only the desktop Office apps
Office 365 E1, which provides web/mobile Office and online services but no desktop apps or Intune
questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 Business Premium is built for organizations up to 300 seats and bundles Office desktop apps, Exchange/Teams/SharePoint, Intune and Defender for Business — typically the most cost-effective SMB fit. M365 E5 is far pricier than needed at this scale. Apps for Enterprise has no email or device management. Office 365 E1 has no desktop apps and no Intune.

questions.q: Which Microsoft 365 Enterprise plan is required to obtain Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2, Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (Premium), Power BI Pro, and Teams Phone all in a single license?
choices: Microsoft 365 E1, which includes web Office and online services without advanced security
Microsoft 365 F3, the frontline-worker SKU without advanced security or Power BI Pro
Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise, which is desktop Office apps only
Microsoft 365 E5, the top enterprise SKU that bundles all of these advanced capabilities
questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 E5 is the top enterprise SKU that bundles Defender for Endpoint Plan 2, Defender for Identity, Purview eDiscovery Premium, Power BI Pro and Teams Phone in one license. E1 has no advanced security or desktop apps. F3 is for frontline workers and omits these advanced tools. Apps for Enterprise is the Office desktop apps only.

questions.q: A retailer wants licenses for warehouse and store staff who only need email, web/mobile Office apps, and basic Teams chat — they share kiosks and don't need full desktop Office. Which plan family is designed for this audience?
choices: Office 365 E5, an information-worker SKU priced well above frontline needs
Microsoft 365 Business Standard, capped at 300 seats and aimed at SMB knowledge workers
Microsoft 365 F1 and F3, the frontline-worker SKUs priced for shift workers on shared devices
Microsoft 365 E3, a full information-worker enterprise plan with desktop Office included
questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 F1 and F3 are the frontline-worker SKUs priced for shift workers who mostly use shared devices and only need essential collaboration — exactly the retail-floor scenario. Office 365 E5 and Microsoft 365 E3 are full information-worker plans, priced higher and tied to a single named user. Business Standard targets SMB knowledge workers and is capped at 300 seats.

questions.q: A customer is comparing Microsoft 365 E3 and Microsoft 365 E5. Which statement accurately captures the difference between the two plans?
choices: E3 includes Teams Phone PSTN calling out of the box; E5 sells it as a separate add-on at higher cost
E5 omits Teams and Exchange Online — those services are exclusive to E3
E3 and E5 are identical in capability and differ only in seat-count pricing tiers
E5 adds advanced security, advanced compliance, Power BI Pro and Teams Phone on top of E3
questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 E3 bundles Office, Windows Enterprise and EMS E3 with baseline security. E5 adds advanced Defender (Endpoint P2, Identity, Cloud Apps), Purview Premium compliance, Power BI Pro and Teams Phone on top of everything in E3. The first three options are factually wrong: Teams Phone is in E5, not E3; E5 still contains Teams and Exchange; and the two plans differ in capability, not only in pricing.

questions.q: A customer wants to lower their per-month cost on Microsoft 365 E3 and is willing to commit for 12 months instead of paying month-to-month. Which billing option provides a discount in exchange for that commitment?
choices: Spot pricing, a short-lived auction discount that is offered for Azure spare compute, not Microsoft 365 seats
Annual commitment subscription, which discounts the per-user price in exchange for a 12-month term
Reserved Capacity for Microsoft 365, which is not a Microsoft 365 commercial offering
Pay-as-you-go consumption pricing, where the customer is billed only for usage with no commitment
questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 commercial plans offer an annual commitment subscription with a discounted per-user price in exchange for the 12-month term. Spot pricing is an Azure VM concept, not an M365 billing option. 'Reserved Capacity for Microsoft 365' does not exist. Pay-as-you-go has no commitment and therefore no commitment discount.

nodes.title: Microsoft support plans: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Microsoft offers tiered support plans for Microsoft 365 and Azure. MS-900 exams test response times, support scope, and what's included in each tier versus the default included support.

flashcards.front: Four Microsoft support plan tiers?
flashcards.back: Developer (dev/test only), Standard (production environments), Professional Direct (business-critical, faster SLAs), Unified (formerly Premier — full enterprise coverage).

flashcards.front: What support is included free with any Microsoft 365 subscription?
flashcards.back: 24/7 online self-help, documentation, community forums, and billing/account management support. Technical break-fix for critical issues is included but with no SLA.

flashcards.front: Professional Direct SLA for critical severity?
flashcards.back: Initial response within 1 hour for Severity A (business-critical outage) — compared to 2 hours for Standard.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Unified support advantage over lower tiers?
flashcards.back: Dedicated Customer Success Account Manager (CSAM), proactive services, on-demand assessments, and custom SLAs — effectively the former Premier Support contract.

questions.q: An enterprise has 500 Microsoft 365 licenses and wants Microsoft engineers to help them plan and deploy Teams, SharePoint, and Intune at no extra cost. Which Microsoft program offers this onboarding assistance?
choices: Microsoft Unified Support, a paid enterprise support contract with proactive services
FastTrack for Microsoft 365, the no-extra-cost onboarding program
Microsoft Consulting Services (MCS), a paid professional-services engagement
Microsoft Premier Support, the predecessor to Unified Support and also a paid offering
questions.explanation: FastTrack for Microsoft 365 is a customer-success program included at no extra cost with eligible subscriptions (typically 150+ licenses); Microsoft engineers help plan, deploy and adopt Microsoft 365 services. Unified Support is a paid enterprise support contract. MCS is a paid consulting engagement. Premier Support is the older paid model that Unified replaced.

questions.q: Where should an admin look for upcoming Microsoft 365 features that are in preview, rolling out, or recently launched, with target dates and categories?
choices: Microsoft Learn Catalog, which lists training modules and learning paths
Microsoft 365 admin center → Billing, which shows licenses and invoices
Microsoft 365 Roadmap, which lists features in development, rolling out and launched with target dates
Microsoft Service Trust Portal, which publishes audit reports and compliance documentation
questions.explanation: The Microsoft 365 Roadmap (microsoft.com/microsoft-365/roadmap) is the public list of features in development, rolling out and recently launched, with target dates and the products affected. Microsoft Learn Catalog is for training modules. The Billing page shows licenses and invoices. The Service Trust Portal publishes compliance and audit documents.

questions.q: Microsoft publishes uptime commitments for Microsoft 365 services. What is the financially backed uptime SLA for most Microsoft 365 services such as Exchange Online and SharePoint Online?
choices: 99.9%, the financially backed monthly uptime commitment for most Microsoft 365 services
99.0%, which would allow about 7 hours of downtime per month and is not the Microsoft 365 commitment
99.999%, a 'five nines' target Microsoft does not contractually guarantee for these services
95.0%, far below Microsoft's published commitments for productivity services
questions.explanation: Most Microsoft 365 services such as Exchange Online and SharePoint Online have a financially backed 99.9% monthly uptime SLA, with service credits if Microsoft fails to meet it. 99.999% is not the contractual figure for these services. 99.0% would allow over seven hours of downtime per month and 95.0% is well below any published Microsoft commitment.

questions.q: An admin wants real-time information about ongoing service incidents affecting their Microsoft 365 tenant (for example, an Outlook on the web outage). Which tool should they consult?
choices: Microsoft Secure Score, which rates the tenant's security posture
Microsoft Compliance Manager, which measures regulatory and compliance posture
Service Health page in the Microsoft 365 admin center, which reports current incidents
Microsoft 365 Roadmap, which lists upcoming and recently released features
questions.explanation: The Service Health page in the Microsoft 365 admin center reports active incidents and advisories affecting the tenant, including impact, status and remediation timelines. Secure Score measures security posture. Compliance Manager measures regulatory posture. The Roadmap describes upcoming feature releases, not live outages.

questions.q: An enterprise customer with thousands of seats wants a dedicated Customer Success Account Manager and a contractual response time for Sev A incidents under 1 hour. Which Microsoft support offering meets this?
choices: FastTrack for Microsoft 365, which provides onboarding and adoption help but not 24/7 reactive support
Microsoft Unified Support, an enterprise support contract with a named CSAM
Microsoft Learn Premium, which is a training catalog rather than a support contract
The basic support included with a Microsoft 365 subscription, which does not provide a dedicated CSAM
questions.explanation: Microsoft Unified Support (which replaced Premier Support) is the enterprise support contract that provides a Customer Success Account Manager, proactive services and contractual response times for the highest-severity incidents. FastTrack is for deployment, not reactive support. Microsoft Learn Premium is training. Basic included support gives no dedicated CSAM and no contractual response time.

nodes.title: Microsoft Teams: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Microsoft Teams is the hub for teamwork in Microsoft 365, combining chat, meetings, calling, and app integration. MS-900 exams test Teams architecture, guest access, compliance controls, and licensing.

flashcards.front: Teams channel vs chat — key difference?
flashcards.back: Channels are persistent, team-wide conversation threads stored in SharePoint. Chats are private 1:1 or group conversations stored in Exchange mailboxes.

flashcards.front: Guest access vs external access in Teams?
flashcards.back: Guest access: external users join a specific Team and get access to channels/files (requires an Azure AD guest account). External access: federate with another Teams tenant for chat/calls only — no team membership.

flashcards.front: Teams Direct Routing — purpose?
flashcards.back: Connect a customer-managed Session Border Controller (SBC) to Teams Phone, letting users make PSTN calls through an existing telephony provider without a Microsoft Calling Plan.

flashcards.front: Which Microsoft 365 licence is required for Teams?
flashcards.back: Teams is included in Microsoft 365 Business Basic and above, and Office 365 E1 and above. A free Teams (Essentials) tier exists with limited features and no Microsoft 365 integration.

questions.q: A project team wants a single workspace that combines persistent chat, file sharing, video meetings, and tabs for third-party apps. Which Microsoft 365 service best meets this need?
choices: Microsoft Outlook on the web, the browser client for Exchange Online mail and calendaring
Microsoft Stream, the video hosting and streaming service for organizations
Microsoft Planner, a lightweight task and Kanban-board service
Microsoft Teams, the hub for chat, channels, meetings and integrated app tabs
questions.explanation: Microsoft Teams is the workspace that bundles persistent chat, channel-based file sharing (backed by SharePoint), meetings, calling and pluggable tabs for third-party apps. Outlook on the web is an email client. Microsoft Stream is for video hosting. Planner provides task boards but has no chat, meetings or file workspace.

questions.q: A team wants to co-author a portable component containing a task list and table that can live inside a Teams chat, an Outlook email, and a Word document at the same time. Which Microsoft 365 capability provides this?
choices: Microsoft Loop, with live components that synchronize wherever they are pasted
Microsoft 365 Groups, which provide shared membership but not portable in-line components
SharePoint web parts, embeddable building blocks limited to SharePoint pages
Teams adaptive cards, interactive UI elements scoped to a single Teams message
questions.explanation: Microsoft Loop components are live tables, lists and paragraphs that stay in sync wherever they are pasted — Teams, Outlook, Word for the web and Whiteboard. Microsoft 365 Groups define shared mail, calendar and file membership; they're not portable in-line content. SharePoint web parts only live on SharePoint pages. Adaptive cards are interactive UI elements rendered inside one Teams message, not a co-authored shared component.

questions.q: A small clinic wants customers to self-book appointments with specific staff members and receive automatic email confirmations. Which Microsoft 365 service provides this booking page?
choices: Microsoft Forms, a survey and quiz tool with no scheduling logic
Microsoft Lists, a structured-data tracking app with no booking page
Microsoft Bookings, a self-service appointment-scheduling page
Microsoft Planner, a Kanban-style task tracker for teams
questions.explanation: Microsoft Bookings publishes a customer-facing booking page tied to staff calendars and sends confirmation and reminder emails automatically. Forms creates surveys and quizzes. Lists tracks structured data such as inventory or issues. Planner manages tasks across a team; none of those three exposes a self-service appointment page.

questions.q: An organization needs to obtain phone numbers and PSTN dial-in / dial-out capability for Microsoft Teams users. Which add-on must be licensed?
choices: Skype for Business Server CAL, a legacy on-premises license that does not apply to Teams Phone
Microsoft Bookings Premium, an appointment-scheduling product that does not provide PSTN calling
Microsoft 365 Audio Conferencing, which provides dial-in for meetings but not full PSTN outbound calling
Microsoft Teams Phone with a Calling Plan, Operator Connect or Direct Routing for PSTN access
questions.explanation: Microsoft Teams Phone enables enterprise voice inside Teams; to actually make and receive PSTN calls you pair it with a Microsoft Calling Plan, Operator Connect or Direct Routing using your own SBC. Skype for Business Server CAL is a legacy on-prem license and doesn't apply. Bookings Premium has nothing to do with telephony. Audio Conferencing only provides dial-in for meetings, not full outbound PSTN calling.

nodes.title: Mixed exam topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Some exam objectives don't fit neatly into a single domain — they span protocols, tools, or concepts covered briefly in multiple sections. These cards treat each item as a stand-alone fact, the way an exam question presents it: one concept, one answer.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between a hub, a switch, and a router?
flashcards.back: Hub: Layer 1, repeats every frame to all ports — all devices share bandwidth, collisions guaranteed. Switch: Layer 2, forwards frames using a MAC address table to only the destination port — full duplex, no collisions, each port gets full bandwidth. Router: Layer 3, makes forwarding decisions based on IP address, connects different networks. Hub is legacy; switches dominate LAN; routers are at network edges.

flashcards.front: What is RAID 5 and how many drives can it tolerate losing?
flashcards.back: RAID 5 stripes data and parity across at least 3 drives. Any single drive failure can be recovered by reconstructing missing data from the remaining drives and parity. It cannot tolerate 2 simultaneous drive failures. Effective capacity = (N-1) × drive size. Read performance is excellent; write requires parity recalculation. RAID 6 tolerates 2 failures using double parity.

flashcards.front: What does a proxy server do, and how does a forward proxy differ from a reverse proxy?
flashcards.back: Forward proxy: sits between clients and the internet on behalf of clients — used for content filtering, caching, and anonymizing outbound requests (the server sees the proxy's IP). Reverse proxy: sits in front of servers on behalf of the server — used for load balancing, SSL termination, caching, and hiding backend topology (the client sees the proxy's IP). Both intermediate HTTP, but they protect opposite sides.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of a DMZ in network architecture?
flashcards.back: A demilitarized zone is a network segment between the untrusted internet and the trusted internal network, typically protected by two firewalls (or two interfaces on one firewall). Public-facing services (web, email, DNS) sit in the DMZ: internet can reach them but not the internal network; if the DMZ host is compromised, the inner firewall still blocks access to the internal LAN.

questions.q: An organization wants a curated employee experience platform inside Teams that surfaces company news, resources, and personalized dashboards. Which Microsoft Viva module addresses this?
choices: Viva Topics, which uses AI to organize knowledge into topic pages from existing content
Viva Connections, the personalized employee gateway inside Teams
Viva Learning, which aggregates training content from multiple providers inside Teams
Viva Insights, which provides personal wellbeing and productivity analytics
questions.explanation: Viva Connections is the Teams-embedded employee gateway: it surfaces curated news, a customizable dashboard and quick links into a company intranet experience. Viva Topics is a knowledge-mining service that auto-builds topic pages — not a personalized news feed. Viva Learning focuses on training content. Viva Insights focuses on individual wellbeing and productivity rather than a company-wide gateway.

questions.q: An organization wants employees to ask company-wide questions and get answers from senior leaders in a Yammer-style social network. Which Viva module supports this?
choices: Viva Learning, which curates training courses from internal and external sources
Viva Insights, which provides personal and manager-level wellbeing analytics
Viva Topics, which auto-builds topic pages from existing content
Viva Engage, the Yammer-based community and leadership-Q&A experience
questions.explanation: Viva Engage is the rebranded Yammer experience for company-wide communities, leadership conversations and storyline posts. Viva Learning surfaces training. Viva Insights focuses on wellbeing and focus time. Viva Topics builds topic pages from documents — none of those three is the social-Q&A surface the question describes.

questions.q: An organization wants to assign and track Word, Excel, and PowerPoint training courses from LinkedIn Learning, Microsoft Learn, and internal SharePoint sources directly inside Teams. Which Viva module fits?
choices: Viva Insights, which surfaces personal productivity and focus-time analytics
Viva Connections, the personalized employee-experience gateway inside Teams
Viva Goals, which manages objectives and key results (OKRs)
Viva Learning, which aggregates training content from multiple providers inside Teams
questions.explanation: Viva Learning pulls courses from providers such as LinkedIn Learning, Microsoft Learn and internal SharePoint libraries into one Teams app where employees can find, share and complete them. Viva Insights surfaces analytics, not learning content. Viva Connections is a personalized intranet gateway. Viva Goals tracks OKRs.

questions.q: A company wants to give employees a way to record their personal goals, key results, and progress aligned to business objectives, with check-ins and dashboards. Which Microsoft Viva module addresses this?
choices: Viva Topics, which mines content to organize knowledge into topic pages
Viva Pulse, which collects quick sentiment surveys from teams
Viva Goals, which manages objectives and key results (OKRs) with check-ins and dashboards
Viva Insights, which provides personal and manager-level productivity analytics
questions.explanation: Viva Goals is the OKR-management module: it lets teams set objectives and key results, check in on progress and surface dashboards aligned to business objectives. Viva Topics auto-builds topic pages from content. Viva Pulse collects sentiment surveys. Viva Insights provides productivity analytics, not goal tracking.

questions.q: A Microsoft 365 admin wants to enforce passwordless sign-in using a mobile authenticator app for all users. Which Microsoft service implements this identity capability?
choices: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD), the cloud identity provider for Microsoft 365
Microsoft Defender for Identity, an AD-focused threat-detection service
Microsoft Purview Information Protection, which classifies and encrypts content
Microsoft Intune compliance policies, which evaluate device posture but do not issue credentials
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID is the identity provider behind Microsoft 365 and supports passwordless sign-in via Microsoft Authenticator, FIDO2 security keys and Windows Hello. Defender for Identity detects on-prem AD attacks, not how users sign in. Purview Information Protection labels and encrypts content. Intune compliance policies evaluate devices for conditional access but don't issue user credentials.

questions.q: An organization wants users to be challenged with multifactor authentication only when they sign in from outside the corporate network or from a non-compliant device. Which Entra ID feature enforces this rule?
choices: Self-service password reset, which lets users reset their own passwords
Privileged Identity Management (PIM), which provides just-in-time elevation of admin roles
Identity Secure Score, a posture rating with recommended improvements
Conditional Access policies, which evaluate sign-in signals and can require MFA
questions.explanation: Conditional Access policies evaluate sign-in signals — user, location, device compliance, risk — and conditionally require MFA or block access. Self-service password reset lets users recover their own passwords. PIM elevates admins just-in-time. Identity Secure Score is a posture rating, not an enforcement engine.

questions.q: An admin needs to grant a user the Global Administrator role only for a 4-hour change window, requiring approval and audit logging. Which Entra ID feature enables this just-in-time elevation?
choices: Self-service group management, which lets users request membership in groups
Conditional Access named locations, which describe trusted network ranges
Identity Protection sign-in risk policy, which responds to risky sign-ins
Privileged Identity Management (PIM), which provides just-in-time role activation
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) provides just-in-time, time-bound, approval-gated activation of privileged roles with full auditing — included with Entra ID P2. Self-service group management is unrelated to role activation. Named locations only define network ranges for Conditional Access. Identity Protection sign-in risk policy responds to risky sign-ins, not on-demand role elevation.

questions.q: Which authentication method is considered the strongest passwordless option for Microsoft Entra ID, providing phishing-resistant credentials backed by hardware?
choices: Security questions, a weak knowledge-based factor
SMS-based one-time passwords, which are susceptible to SIM swaps and phishing
Email-based one-time passcodes, also susceptible to interception and phishing
FIDO2 security keys, which provide hardware-backed phishing-resistant credentials
questions.explanation: FIDO2 security keys (along with Windows Hello for Business and certificate-based authentication) provide hardware-backed, phishing-resistant passwordless authentication. Security questions are weak knowledge-based factors. SMS and email one-time passcodes can be intercepted or phished and are not phishing-resistant.
